Apple iPhone.Online Prices: Those online prices lose about 15% to seller fees before shipping, and you're carrying the scam risk. I can hand you cash today.
Apple iPhone.Battery Health [X]%: It's showing [X]% battery health, so whoever buys it next is replacing the battery pretty soon — that comes off what I can offer.
Apple iPhone.Base Storage: This is the base storage model. Buyers are asking for more space now, so these sit on the shelf a lot longer.
Apple iPhone.Carrier Locked: Because it's still locked to that carrier, I can only sell it to someone on that same carrier. That's a much smaller pool of buyers.
Apple iPhone.Micro-Scratches: The screen isn't cracked, you're right — but with these scratches I have to list it as Fair instead of Mint, and that's a real price difference.
Apple iPhone.Untested Item: Since I can't fully test this one, I have to price in the chance it needs more work than I can see right now.
Apple iPhone.Store Credit Pivot: If the cash number isn't working for you, I can do $[X] in store credit right now toward anything in the store.

Apple iPad.WiFi-Only: This is the WiFi-only model — no GPS and no cellular. It's a less flexible tablet, and that shows up in what it resells for.
Apple iPad.Battery Wear: The battery in these is sealed in, so servicing it is a real job. High wear means the next owner is facing that cost.
Apple iPad.White Spots: Those light patches on the screen are backlight damage — it's a permanent hardware fault, not something that cleans up.
Apple iPad.OS Updates: This generation is at the end of Apple's support window, so apps will start dropping off it. That makes it a slow seller for me.
Apple iPad.Base Storage: At this storage size buyers hesitate — most people want 128GB or more now.

Apple Smart Watch.Battery Health: The battery in these is tiny, and this one's worn down enough that the next owner won't get through a full day on it.
Apple Smart Watch.Casing Wear: A watch is jewelry — people look at it. Scratches on the screen and pitting in the aluminum cost more here than they would on a phone.
Apple Smart Watch.Outdated Tech: The sensors and processor in this generation are a few years behind now, and that's where the demand went.
Apple Smart Watch.Base Model: This is the aluminum GPS-only version, which is the entry model — it doesn't bring what a Stainless or an Ultra does.
Apple Smart Watch.Band Hygiene: The band is worn and discolored, and for hygiene I have to replace it before it goes back out. That cost is in my number.
Apple Smart Watch.Charger Missing: The charger for these is proprietary and pricey, so not having the original changes what I can do.
Apple Smart Watch.SE Series: This is the SE line. It doesn't have the always-on display or the health sensors the main series has, and resale reflects that.

Apple MacBooks.Intel Processor: This one's an Intel model, and Apple moved to their own M-series chips a while back. The Intels run hotter and slower, and buyers know it.
Apple MacBooks.High Cycle Count: Mac batteries are rated to about 1,000 cycles and this one's well past that, so a battery service is coming for whoever buys it.
Apple MacBooks.8GB RAM: It's the 8GB model. Anyone doing real work on it wants 16 at a minimum now, so this one moves slowly.
Apple MacBooks.Case Dents: Dents in the aluminum can't be worked out — they're permanent. On a premium machine like this, that hits the resale price hard.
Apple MacBooks.Genuine Chargers: The original Apple charger isn't with it, and those aren't cheap to replace — I have to account for buying one.
Apple MacBooks.Butterfly Keyboard: This is one of the 2016 to 2019 models with the butterfly keyboard. They have a known failure history, so demand on them is soft.
Apple MacBooks.Flexgate/Display: See these faint lines along the bottom of the screen? That's a display cable starting to fail, and it gets worse, not better.

GPU.Generational Drop: New card generations come out constantly, and this one's a few behind — it struggles with what people are playing now.
GPU.Thermal Wear: Heavy gaming dries out the thermal paste and wears the fans down, so I'm pricing in the chance this one runs hot.
GPU.Market Saturation: There are a lot of used cards out there right now. That much supply pushes the cash value down for everybody.
GPU.Missing Adapters: This card needs a specific high-wattage power adapter and it isn't here — I have to deduct what it costs to source one.
GPU.Physical Sag: See how the bracket's bent from the card sagging? That's long-term structural stress, and it drops the grade to Fair.
GPU.Coil Whine: It's got a noticeable buzz under load. PC builders hear that immediately and pass, so it's a hard resell.
GPU.No Original Box: Without the original foam packaging, shipping a card this size safely means buying real materials for it.
